clue.text: Clipped Alfa Romeo key ring outside

indicators.note: a clipped word has had its tail trimmed, so the last letter of Alfa goes

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A car owner describes the shortened key ring hanging from an Alfa Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alfa Romeo' looks like the car brand but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doing something in the open air, such as eating outdoors, is doing it al fresco.

clue.text: Nadal latterly storms through Eastbourne's outsiders, creating talk around court

indicators.note: latterly points to the final letter of the tennis player's name
the storms run through the middle, so the two outside letters enclose them
the outsiders of the town's name are its first and last letters

parts.note: storms are gales

explanation.surface: Rafael Nadal plays through bad weather at the Eastbourne tennis tournament, and the gossip spreads around the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like tennis but means a court of law. Eastbourne is a south-coast English town with a grass-court tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal jargon is the language lawyers use in court, so a lawcourt's talk fits the term.

clue.text: One month in first-class college, germ-free

indicators.note: the month and the one are placed in between the first-class and college letters

parts.note: A is the grade for first-class, as in A1
Sept is the short form of September
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A student spends a month at a top college that is perfectly hygienic.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads first-class as AI (A1) holding the month, then C; this parse uses every word, with One as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sterile surgical environment free of harmful bacteria is called aseptic.

clue.text: Fabulous dog, porky around backside

indicators.note: the falsehood is wrapped around the rear end

parts.note: porky (pork pie) is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie
ass is a slang word for the backside

explanation.surface: A legendary dog that is rather fat around its rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porky' looks like 'fat' but is rhyming slang: pork pie = lie. 'Fabulous' means legendary, of fable or film.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the famous collie of books, film and television is a legendary canine.

clue.text: Swinging family, one seen in minimal clothing

parts.note: swinging both ways sexually means bisexual, shortened to bi
your kin are your family
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A swinging family, one member wearing hardly anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a two-piece swimsuit is the classic skimpy garment worn on beaches.

clue.text: Limousines monarch requires at sporting activity

parts.note: Rollers is slang for Rolls-Royce cars, the classic luxury limousines

indicators.note: requires is read as 'holds within', so the monarch takes the word at inside

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A king insists on limousines for some sporting outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: gliding on wheeled boots is a recreational sport and pastime.

clue.text: Dress right, with German mate (film actor)

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown
mit is the German word for with
a chum is a mate or friend

explanation.surface: Instructions to dress properly alongside a German friend, with a film actor named in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with German' is a single instruction: the German for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American star of Cape Fear and The Night of the Hunter was a Hollywood leading man.

clue.text: Sticky stuff on green? Notice golf executives initially become furious

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
vert is green in heraldry
to heed is to notice or take note
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word executives

explanation.surface: Something sticky on the putting green makes golf executives lose their temper when they notice it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests a golf course but is the heraldic colour vert.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: losing control entirely, flying into a rage, is described as tipping beyond the brink.

clue.text: African country loses lake and peninsula northwards

indicators.note: loses tells us to drop the lake's letter from the country's name

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An African country loses a lake, and there is a peninsula to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' belongs with the definition: the peninsula lies north of Africa across the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: Spain and Portugal share the landmass lying north of Africa, across the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Runner falls over, drinking maritime spirit

parts.note: a runner is a river, and the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the word for falls round

parts.note: to fall in battle is to die, so falls means dies
someone on the bottle is drinking, so on stands for drinking

explanation.surface: A runner takes a tumble while drinking spirits at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete but is a river; 'spirit' looks like alcohol but means a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: the Greek god of the sea is a divine being ruling the oceans.

clue.text: Hire out Alpine house, neglecting tea

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so the tea is dropped from the house

parts.note: a chalet is a wooden house in the Alps
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone renting out a ski chalet forgets to provide tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rent property to a tenant is to hire it out.

clue.text: Tiny bird briefly hides behind fish

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the shortened bird holds the rump
briefly means cut short, so the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: the wren is a tiny brown bird
ass is slang for one's behind

explanation.surface: A tiny bird hides behind a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word but is a noun: the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brightly coloured reef species, some of which clean other sea creatures.

clue.text: Type of statement from record company — it's peripherally edited

indicators.note: peripherally places the letters of it's around the outside of the label's name

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe
EMI is a well-known British record company

explanation.surface: A statement issued by a record label, which says it has been lightly edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripherally' looks like it modifies 'edited' but tells us it's goes round EMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: a bill or bank account summary listing every charge separately is the detailed kind.

clue.text: Quack by duck or noise by animal?

parts.note: quack is slang for a doctor, and MO is a medical officer
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether a quack is the duck's noise or another animal's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' seems to be the duck's call but means a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lowing call of a cow is a farmyard sound.

clue.text: Authorise energy company to get name replaced by mid-November

indicators.note: replaced by tells us the name's letter is swapped out for the central letters of the month

parts.note: npower is a UK electricity and gas supplier

indicators.note: mid- points to the two middle letters of the month

explanation.surface: An energy firm changes its name in November to gain authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to give someone the power or right to act is to authorise them.

clue.text: How backstroke contestant ends

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: How does a backstroke swimmer finish the race?
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a swimmer leaves the pool soaked through with water.

clue.text: Crown controls rifle certificate

indicators.note: controls is read as holds in check, so the head contains the theft

parts.note: the crown of the head is the pate
to rifle a place is to rob it

explanation.surface: The Crown keeps a firearms licence in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: Law: the official document confirming a will's validity is granted by a court.

clue.text: Security guard on night patrol primarily eats Mexican food

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the initials enclose the food
primarily picks the opening letters of night and patrol

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla

explanation.surface: A guard on the night shift mainly eats Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a hired private guard, rather than a real police officer, is mocked with this term.

clue.text: Awful spelling? Deficiency in graduate report's disheartening

indicators.note: the shortfall is set inside the graduate's letters

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
a lack is a deficiency

indicators.note: removing the heart of report leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A graduate's report shows dreadful spelling and is disheartening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' means casting spells, not orthography; 'Awful' means inspiring dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: sinister sorcery, casting evil spells, is dreadful magic.

clue.text: Unoccupied City lecturer invited in once to play twister

indicators.note: unoccupied means emptied of its contents, leaving the outer letters of City
the lecturer's letter is invited in among the letters of once
to play suggests the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: An empty City where a lecturer was once invited to play Twister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twister' looks like the party game but means a whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a violent rotating storm is called a twister in American usage.

clue.text: Retired hooker, say, probes extremely shady tactics

indicators.note: probes means pushes into, so the pieces go inside the outer letters
extremely picks the outermost letters of shady
retired means withdrawn, read as going backwards

parts.note: a tart is slang for a prostitute
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A retired prostitute investigates some rather shady tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' could suggest rugby but is the slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an overall plan of action for achieving an aim is closely related to tactics.

clue.text: Dawn gets two golds, the second in Argentina

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the second gold goes in the country's code

parts.note: RA is the international vehicle registration code for Argentina
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Dawn wins two gold medals, the second in Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second' is the second gold, OR, not the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the Latin name for the goddess of daybreak, used for the first light.

clue.text: Musical brothers see conducting minister uplifted

indicators.note: conducting means carrying within, so the see holds the minister

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue reads the minister's title upward, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: Musical brothers watch a minister conduct an uplifting service.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Don and Phil were an American singing duo of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Groom exhausted by end of honeymoon

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of honeymoon

parts.note: food that is exhausted has been used up, eaten

explanation.surface: A bridegroom worn out by the close of the honeymoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the bridegroom but is the verb to tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to groom something is to tidy it up and make it trim.

clue.text: Leo caught both sides of argument

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: both sides of picks the first and last letters of argument

explanation.surface: Leo was caught on both sides of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like a man's name but is the lion of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lion, the zodiac sign's animal, is a big feline.

clue.text: Lady's OK residing on cloudy river in Midlands

parts.note: c is the weather-map symbol for cloudy

explanation.surface: A woman is fine living by a river under cloudy skies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'residing on' sets the woman's pieces after C in this across clue. The river flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: a Thames tributary flowing south through Banbury and Oxford in central England.

clue.text: Janitor regularly assumes leather for self-protection

clue.text: 'Actress: My Role in Norma's Split'
